intro: Here, ten thousand years of human story wait in a single building. You are in Aksaray Museum, in Aksaray province, which moved to its present home in 2011. Its collection runs from the Neolithic levels of Aşıklı Höyük to the Byzantine burials of the Ihlara valley, and it holds one of Anatolia's lesser known sets of mummies.
history: The museum moved into its present building in 2011. Its story begins at Aşıklı Höyük, where a hunter-gatherer community settled ten thousand years ago. From there it continues through the Byzantine burials of the Ihlara valley, and it ends with the material of the Seljuk caravan road.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Finds from Aşıklı Höyük and the Ihlara mummies. Then move on to the Seljuk works, and finish with the Coin collection.
facts: Did you know? A woman's skeleton from Aşıklı Höyük carries the earliest known trace of brain surgery. The bone around the opening in her skull had begun to heal, so she lived on afterwards. Think of that. And the collection as a whole spans ten thousand years, from Neolithic Aşıklı Höyük to the Seljuk caravan road.
outro: This brings our tour of Aksaray Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these finds stay safe for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
